--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.layout_bfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Place the nodes in layers by breadth-first distance from a start node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.layout_bfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Place the nodes in layers by breadth-first distance from a start node. title: >- [Graph.layout_bfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Place the nodes in layers by breadth-first distance from a start node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Place the nodes in layers by breadth-first distance from a start node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6483-L6609){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.layout_bfs( source, align="vertical", scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![BFS layout](../assets/graphs/layout-bfs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, an eight-node graph scattered at random, node 1 outlined as the start. On the right, layout_bfs(source=1) puts node 1 in the leftmost column and every other node in a column by its distance from node 1, so the graph reads as layers of a breadth-first search." width="100%"} The start node forms the first layer, its neighbors the second, their unvisited neighbors the third, and so on; the layers are then drawn as in `layout_multipartite()`, side by side (or one above another with `align="horizontal"`), centered and scaled so the largest coordinate is `scale=`. Within a layer, nodes keep the order the search reached them in, visiting neighbors in ID order. Directed graphs are searched along edge directions. This matches NetworkX's `bfs_layout()`. Breadth-first layers make trees and shallow hierarchies readable and show how far each node is from a chosen root, such as a source in a flow network or a seed account in a social graph. Every node must be reachable from `source=`. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID or label to start from. [align]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["vertical"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"vertical"` (default) for vertical layers side by side, or `"horizontal"` for horizontal layers one above another. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest coordinate after rescaling. Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the layout, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If some node can't be reached from `source=`, `align=` is unknown, or `scale=` or `center=` is invalid. [NodeNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` doesn't exist. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~bfs_layers`) : List the nodes at each distance from a start node. [](`~layout_multipartite`) : Place nodes in parallel lines, one per layer. [](`~to_undirected`) : Make an undirected copy of the graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A breadth-first search from `source=` puts each node in a layer by its distance from the source. In a company's reporting lines, starting from the chief executive, Mira, makes each column a level of management: ::: {#9e1163f2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec org = ec.org_chart().layout_bfs(source="Mira") org.plot(layout="pos", label_by="label", width=820, height=480) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### How far from the intern The search follows the edges' directions, which run from managers to their reports, so a search from Noor, the intern, reaches no one and raises an error. In the undirected copy, the layers count the reporting lines between each person and Noor. The path to anyone outside engineering runs up through Mira, and the furthest, 9 lines away, is Ada in finance: ::: {#b4eecbaf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ties = ec.org_chart().to_undirected() ties.layout_bfs(source="Noor") ties.plot(layout="pos", label_by="label", width=820, height=480) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Layouts](../user-guide/layouts.qmd#layered-layouts) draws a small organization in layers from the top down.
